correctness.rationale: For every Haar two-plane the projected orthotope is a zonotope with perimeter twice the sum of projected edge lengths. The rank-two projection matrix gives diagonal moments 2/d and a beta marginal. Stabilizer conditioning reduces the distinct-axis length product to the norm of a two-coordinate projection of a uniform sphere vector in the d-1 dimensional complement. Independent beta radius and uniform angle then yield a Gauss 2F1 angular integral, and an exact Euler beta-series calculation yields pi*3F2(-1/2,1/2,3/2;1,(d+1)/2;1)/(2(d-1)). Expanding the square proves the orthotope formula. A beta-weighted hypergeometric Taylor remainder is O(d^-2) and the gamma-ratio expansion proves the 8-5pi/2 variance limit. The executable package checks independent numeric integrals, convex hull perimeters and Haar simulation; no finite experiment is used as the universal proof.
risks: The proof uses Haar-uniform orthogonal Grassmannian subspaces, not Gaussian nonorthogonal projections.
The high-dimensional limit is for variance only, without any distributional convergence assertion.

originality.rationale: The primary 2015 geometry-classified work solves all-dimension moments of ONE-dimensional projected widths, but the two-plane perimeter second moment requires an additional off-diagonal covariance kernel. Finch 2012 gives the same 3-cube hypergeometric formula and a numerical 4-cube result, whereas this claim gives an evaluated all-d and arbitrary-orthotope expression plus nonzero high-dimensional variance limit. Paouris-Pivovarov-Zinn compute distributions and asymptotics for the projected two-dimensional area, not perimeter. Actual text and semantic searches under mathematical equivalents yielded no implication-equivalent all-d formula. Unindexed random-zonotope work and inaccessible broader moment sources remain residual risks.
residual_risks: An older or unindexed random-zonotope calculation may contain the same all-dimensional correlation reduction.

value.rationale: Planar-shadow perimeter is the canonical projected first intrinsic volume, and its orientation variance quantifies how a box image changes under random viewing angle. An exact squared-perimeter law was numerically tabulated for the four-cube in the initiating research literature but not evaluated uniformly in dimension. The new result treats every side-length tuple in all dimensions, supplies a reusable mixed moment of lengths of two perpendicular projected edges, resolves the four-cube exact expression, and finds a nonzero limiting cube-variance constant. This is a complete natural family classification of a quantitatively motivated higher-order integral-geometric invariant rather than a routine low-dimensional table entry.
risks: No theorem is claimed beyond orthogonal boxes, and no broad CLT or distributional statement follows merely from a variance limit.
